comments.body: Have you tried the suggestion in the following comment? https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2088?focusedCommentId=50980&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-50980

I am unclear on what the intention of this ticket is. There never has been a restriction on the number of fcrepo-camel instances running in Karaf (nor is there one now). There is a restriction on the number of fcrepo-camel-toolbox applications that can be deployed – e.g. one instance of a given version of fcrepo-reindexer or fcrepo-indexing-triplestore, but there has always been that restriction. If you are writing custom camel routes, then this is, again, not an issue – you can point camel at however many different fedora instances as you want.

From the conversation on https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2088 it sounds like this is possible by configuration, but it is not clear about how to do it.

What we need to do is using the same route with two different Fedora endpoints, possibly not duplicating the whole workflow. Our test Camel instance is used to update both our test and development environments and FCREPO-2088 Closed breaks this.

Can someone add some documentation in this regard (provided my assumption that this is attainable by configuration is correct)?

The conversation in FCREPO-2088 Closed is somewhat orthogonal to this, but once fcrepo-camel 4.5.0 is released, it will be completely moot. By way of explanation, the current camel infrastructure uses JMS headers that consist of an identifier and a baseUrl. By assembling these, a Fedora URL can be constructed for a resource. And mostly, the baseURL is assumed to be equivalent to the fcrepo-camel endpoint URI. With fcrepo-camel 4.5.0 that structure will still be supported, but users will be encouraged to make use of a single URI. This is all in line with the draft messaging specification. As such, a single route can access any number of Fedora instances like so:

from("activemq:queue:fedora").routeId("FedoraRouter")
    .process(new EventProcessor())
    .choose()
        .when(header(FCREPO_URI).startsWith("http://test-repo.example.org"))
            .to("direct:test-stuff")
        .when(header(FCREPO_URI).startsWith("http://dev-repo.example.org"))
            .to("direct:dev-stuff")
        .when(header(FCREPO_URI).startsWith("http://repo.example.org"))
            .to("direct:production-stuff");

from("direct:test-stuff")
    .filter(not(header(FCREPO_EVENT_TYPE).contains(DELETED)))
        .to("fcrepo:localhost?authUsername=testUser&authPassword=testPass")
        .to("direct:something-else");

from("direct:production-stuff")
    .filter(not(header(FCREPO_EVENT_TYPE).contains(DELETED)))
        .to("fcrepo:localhost?authUsername=productionUser&authPassword=productionPass")
        .to("direct:something-else");
Closing this, based on kefo's comment above.
